title: Adalo Review 2026: Features, Pros, and Cons
summary: Adalo actually publishes native apps to the App Store and Google Play, which most no-code tools cannot. The ceilings to understand first are records, user counts and the complete absence of code export.
body_markdown:
*Reviewed September 26, 2026. This is a research-based review of Adalo's official pricing and published customer feedback — not a hands-on benchmark. Jet Admin publishes this comparison and is a competing product; competitor strengths are stated as found.*


Adalo is worth considering when you need a real mobile app in the App Store or Google Play and cannot build one. Its strongest advantage is exactly that: most no-code competitors stop at a web app, and Adalo does not. The trade-off is a set of hard ceilings — records per collection, user counts and performance — plus no way to export what you build.


This review covers what Adalo delivers, the ceilings that decide whether it suits your project, what reviewers report, current pricing and how it compares with Jet Admin.


## Adalo review: the quick verdict


Adalo suits small consumer or community apps that genuinely need store distribution and will stay modest in size. It is a weaker fit for data-heavy applications, growing user bases, or anything you may need to take elsewhere.


Strong reasons to consider Adalo Trade-offs to evaluate


Publishes to the App Store and Google Play, not just web Reported ~10,000 records per collection before Android performance degrades


Beginner-friendly drag-and-drop; ship something in minutes Zero code export — leaving means a complete rebuild


Unlimited app actions on paid plans, no usage-based charges Reviewers report problems beyond roughly 5,000 users


Free tier is genuinely useful for prototyping Mixed ratings and reports of slow support and price rises


No numerical score is given, because we did not run a scored hands-on evaluation.


## What is Adalo?


Adalo is a no-code app builder that produces both web and native mobile apps. You design screens on a blank canvas, define collections for data, wire up actions, and publish — including to the Apple and Google stores.


The store publishing is the whole reason to choose it. Tools like Softr and Glide produce web apps you can add to a phone's home screen; Adalo produces something you submit for review and list. If your requirement is genuinely "an app in the store," that narrows the field dramatically, and Adalo is on the short list.


## Adalo's key features


### 1. Native publishing to app stores


Paid plans from Starter publish to both web and app stores, with custom domains included. This is the differentiator, and it is worth confirming your app meets store review requirements before committing.


### 2. Blank-canvas drag-and-drop design


Reviewers describe it as a blank-canvas builder where you can ship a working app in minutes with zero coding. Unlimited screens are available from the free plan onward.


### 3. Collections as the data layer


Adalo provides its own database in the form of collections. The free plan allows 500 records per app, which is enough to prototype and not enough to run anything.


### 4. Unlimited app actions with no usage billing


Every paid tier includes unlimited app actions and no usage-based charges. In a category increasingly metered by credits and workload units, a flat monthly fee with no consumption risk is genuinely attractive.


### 5. Integrations and API access


Reviewers note easy integration with other software on a full API basis. API access appears on the Team plan; custom integrations and geolocation from Professional.


## Adalo pros


### It actually publishes to the stores


This is the reason to use Adalo and it is a real capability, not a marketing claim. For a community app, a small marketplace or an internal app that must be installed, nothing else in the no-code tier does this as directly.


### Beginner-friendly and fast to a first result


Reviewers repeatedly praise how quickly a non-technical person gets something working. Several highlight the free tier as a good way to prototype before paying, which is a sensible sequence given the ceilings below.


### Predictable billing


Unlimited app actions and no usage-based charges mean your monthly cost does not move with success. Compared with workload units or agent credits, this removes a whole category of budgeting risk.


### Annual billing saves 20%


Straightforward and clearly stated, with all headline prices quoted on the annual basis.


## Adalo cons and limitations


### There is a hard performance ceiling on records


Reviewers report roughly 10,000 records per collection before Android performance collapses, and native Android performance lagging well behind the PWA version.


**Who it affects:** any app whose data grows — catalogues, listings, message histories. **Scope:** customer reports, not a documented limit. **What to do:** load a realistic record volume on an Android device early. This is the limit most likely to end an Adalo project after significant investment.


### User growth has a reported ceiling too


One verified reviewer states that beyond roughly 5,000 users you will have to leave Adalo to avoid poor store reviews.


**What to do:** if your plan involves meaningful consumer scale, treat Adalo as a validation tool rather than the destination, and budget for the rebuild explicitly.


### There is no code export at all


Reviewers are unambiguous: no React Native source, no JavaScript, no configuration files are available, and leaving requires a complete rebuild from scratch.


**Who it affects:** anyone whose app succeeds. **What to do:** combined with the ceilings above, this is the central strategic risk. The honest framing is that Adalo is excellent for proving an idea and structurally unsuitable for one that outgrows it — decide which you are doing before you start.


### Support and pricing draw complaints


Reviewers cite developer support as the main drawback, with poor response times and community support needing improvement, alongside significant pricing increases.


### Ratings are genuinely mixed


Unlike most products in this category, Adalo's ratings do not cluster high. See the table below — the picture is a product people enjoy starting with and a smaller group who hit its walls.


## What do Adalo users say?


Source Rating Reviews behind it


[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/adalo/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) 4.4 / 5 7


Product Hunt 3.3 / 5 22


[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/207495/Adalo/reviews) 3.5 / 5 15 (9 would recommend)


All three samples are small, so treat them as indicative. The consistent shape is more informative than the numbers: enthusiasm about speed and accessibility, frustration about scale, support and lock-in.


**Positive themes:** fast and beginner-friendly; ship a working app in minutes; useful free tier; easy integrations on a full API.


**Negative themes:** record and user ceilings; Android performance behind the PWA; zero code export; support responsiveness; price increases.

### When Adalo is the better choice


If store distribution is a genuine requirement and your app will stay small, Adalo does something no application platform in this comparison does. That is a legitimate reason to accept its ceilings.


## Who should use Adalo — and who should compare alternatives?


**Good fit:** small consumer or community apps needing store listing; prototypes validating a mobile idea; single-app projects with one builder; teams wanting predictable flat billing.


**Compare alternatives if:** your data will exceed a few thousand records per collection; you expect more than a few thousand users; your data belongs in an existing database; or you cannot accept a rebuild as the only exit.

## Adalo review FAQ


### What is Adalo?


A no-code builder for web and native mobile apps, with its own database, that can publish to the App Store and Google Play.


### Is Adalo free?


There is a free plan with 500 records per app, unlimited test apps and screens, and one editor — but you cannot publish on it. Starter at $36 a month billed annually is the entry point for a live app.


### Can Adalo really publish to the app stores?


Yes, from the Starter plan upward, to both web and app stores. This is its main differentiator against web-only no-code builders.


### How much data can an Adalo app hold?


Reviewers report performance problems beyond roughly 10,000 records per collection, particularly on Android. Test at your real volume before committing.


### Can I export my Adalo app?


No. Reviewers report no source code, no JavaScript and no configuration files are available, so leaving requires rebuilding from scratch.


### How does Adalo compare with Jet Admin?


Adalo builds store-published apps on its own database; Jet Admin builds operational apps over your existing data with unlimited users. Choose Adalo when store distribution is the requirement.


## Test your record volume on Android first


The single most useful experiment is loading a realistic number of records into a collection and opening the app on an Android device. Adalo's reported ceiling is the limit that ends projects, and the free plan is enough to find it before you pay.


If the app turns out to be an internal tool rather than a store product,[build it on your existing database with Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/) instead.
